newsitem.title: COTE D'IVOIRE: Ivorian yr/yr inflation rises to 6.1 pct in March.
newsitem.headline: Ivorian yr/yr inflation rises to 6.1 pct in March.

text.p: Ivory Coast's year-on-year inflation rose to 6.1 percent in March from 4.9 percent in February, according to provisional figures from the national statistics institute.
The figures showed a rise of 1.5 percent in prices in February, mainly due to an increase in food prices.
The government has said that its target in 1997 is to keep inflation below three percent.
The blue-collar consumer price index (base year November 1992 to October 1993) rose to a provisional 156.3 points in March from 153.8 points in February.
The white-collar consumer price index rose from 144.7 points in February to a provisional 148.0 points in March. The year-on-year inflation rate in March 1996 was 1.6 percent.
Ivory Coast is one of a group of French-speaking countries in Africa that devalued their common CFA franc currency by 50 percent in January 1994.
